page.layout: One page of text, one column with title, verse and signatures. Top left: printed page number "30". Below it: a decorative ornament, then the title of the first poem in two lines (roman capitals and Greek), the poem in four stanzas, the signature "I.I.B.". Then a rule and a second title with its poem, a second signature "I. I. B.", and the catchword "IN" at the lower right. The right edge of the scan cuts off the ends of some title lines.

l.i: VIx praeceps Italis recitarat fama Britanos-
Ecce suis fessos accendunt urbibus ignes-
Atque strepunt latis compita cuncta choris.
Omnibus ipse sua Romanus praesul ab arce-
Non mirum est Italos si mendax fama fagaces-
CUr non dura sua flet funera classis Iberus?
Cur non iusta facit? cur negat exequias?
Barbara gens nescit lachrymas nec iura sepulchri:
Namque illi duro mens adamante riget.

page.notes: The right edge of the scan cuts off the end of the title line "HISPANIS, VETITVM NE..." and the Greek line of the first title; the Greek reading "ωεῷ τῆς" is doubtful. The first letter of the first poem is a large decorated V, read as "VIx". Long s is copied as s throughout. The catchword "IN" sits at the lower right. No running head is printed on this page.
